claim: An LLM can predict mid-generation, via a single extra token, the probability that restarting generation will yield a better response, enabling adaptive best-of-n without an external reward model.
scope_conditions: Llama 3.1 8B, AlpacaEval and GSM8K, general instruction-following and math, not code generation
quoted_support: We use a generative reward model formulation, allowing the LLM to predict mid-generation the probability that restarting the generation will yield a better response.
numbers: win rate 21% to 34% with 16 samples on AlpacaEval

claim: Adaptive stopping based on self-predicted confidence recovers most of the benefit of fixed best-of-16 sampling while using far fewer samples on average.
stance_target: feasibility of confidence-triggered adaptive compute allocation
quoted_support: 74% of the improvement from using 16 samples can be achieved with only 1.2 samples on average.

claim: Early pruning of unpromising samples based on self-predicted confidence can eliminate the majority of samples with minimal performance degradation.
stance_target: feasibility of confidence-triggered adaptive compute allocation
quoted_support: 50-75% of samples can be pruned early in generation with minimal degradation in performance.

claim: This adaptive best-of-n approach operates at whole-response granularity (one confidence prediction per candidate) with no application to code generation or sub-task/requirement-level compute allocation.
stance_target: novelty of per-requirement test-time compute allocation (candidate b)
quoted_support: Best-of-N sampling being a widely used technique. However, this method is computationally expensive, requiring both (1) an external reward model and (2) the generation of multiple samples.
